justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are explicitly covered: Catalog Service with Search Index Manager handles browsing and search; Order & Checkout Service orchestrates cart and checkout with external Payment and Shipping Providers; Review Service handles ratings; and Recommendation Service provides personalized suggestions.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance and scalability are addressed via Global CDN, Distributed Caching Container (ElastiCache Redis with Global Datasets), Redlock cache stampede protection, asynchronous processing through AWS SQS/SNS, and CQRS search indexing in the Catalog Service.
justifications.compatibility: The architecture defines explicit interfaces (REST/JSON, gRPC, AMQP) to integrate external Shipping Providers, multi-currency Payment Gateway, Tax Calculation Service, and SIEM Provider, satisfying all interoperability constraints.
justifications.usability: Customer and Store Administrator personas are catered for via the Single Page Application (SPA) / Mobile Client with State Management & Offline Storage, though administrative capabilities lack dedicated interface components.
justifications.reliability: High availability (99.95%) is targeted using Circuit Breakers, Bulkhead Thread Pools, Saga Orchestrators with Message Outbox, an Idempotency Ledger, health probes, and multi-region replication across Aurora and ElastiCache.
justifications.security: OWASP mitigations and compliance constraints are met via AWS WAF, OAuth2/JWT edge filters, input sanitization middleware, AWS Secrets Manager, and a Cryptographic Erasure Engine (AWS KMS) for GDPR/CCPA user data deletion.
justifications.maintainability: The design enforces high modularity through loosely coupled microservices, database-per-service isolation, clear internal layering (API, Saga, Domain, Infrastructure), and telemetry logging via OpenTelemetry to SIEM.
justifications.portability: The architecture explicitly addresses the required multi-region AWS topology across Aurora and ElastiCache, though heavy reliance on proprietary AWS primitives (KMS, SQS/SNS, Secrets Manager) slightly limits cross-cloud portability.

PERF-01.justification: Global CDN edge caching, ElastiCache with Redlock to prevent stampedes, and a read-optimized CQRS search index absorb high-concurrency traffic during peak catalog browsing.
elements: Global Content Delivery Network (CDN) and WAF
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratios on CDN and Redis during peak surges
Search index read replica capacity and query latency
tradeoffs: Aggressive edge caching improves read latency but risks serving stale catalog data

PERF-02.justification: Recommendation recomputation is decoupled via asynchronous messaging and background processing, while pre-computed cached fallbacks and strict timeouts protect real-time catalog browsing latency.
sensitivity_points: Strict API timeout configuration for recommendation retrieval
Message queue ingestion capacity during batch recomputation
tradeoffs: Serving pre-computed fallbacks preserves browsing performance at the cost of recommendation freshness

AVAIL-01.justification: The checkout orchestrator utilizes the Saga pattern and a transactional message outbox to decouple third-party shipping calls, allowing checkout completion while deferring fulfillment asynchronously.
sensitivity_points: Reliability of the transactional outbox and asynchronous message broker
Shipping provider retry and dead-letter queue policies
tradeoffs: Asynchronous fulfillment allows checkout completion but defers final tracking generation

AVAIL-02.justification: Edge routing combined with Aurora multi-region replication and globally synchronized ElastiCache clusters supports fast regional failover without transaction loss or downtime violating the 99.95% target.
elements: Global Content Delivery Network (CDN) and WAF
sensitivity_points: Cross-region replication latency across Aurora and ElastiCache
DNS and edge router regional failover propagation speed
tradeoffs: Multi-region data replication maintains high availability but introduces cross-region consistency overhead

MOD-01.justification: Payment gateway and tax integrations adapt to currency parameters, but currency conversions across pricing displays and order ledgers lack an explicit independent pricing service.
sensitivity_points: Decoupling of currency formatting and conversion logic across microservices
tradeoffs: Decentralized currency handling simplifies initial design but spreads pricing updates across services

MOD-02.justification: The Recommendation Service encapsulates the ML inference engine behind well-defined REST contracts and asynchronous event consumers, isolating algorithm replacement from all external microservices.
sensitivity_points: Stability of the internal inference engine interfaces and external API contracts
tradeoffs: Encapsulated inference logic ensures service modifiability while restricting client-side recommendation customization

SEC-01.justification: Defense-in-depth via AWS WAF at the edge, API Gateway security filters, input sanitization middleware, and ORM database access effectively neutralizes injection attempts and logs events to SIEM.
elements: Global Content Delivery Network (CDN) and WAF
sensitivity_points: WAF rule coverage and regular expression updates against novel injection vectors
Rigorous parameterized queries across all database repositories
tradeoffs: Deep payload inspection enhances threat detection but introduces slight processing latency overhead

SEC-02.justification: Dedicated anonymization workers and a KMS-driven Cryptographic Erasure Engine in the user data store ensure timely, verifiable personal data deletion to satisfy CCPA and GDPR mandates.
sensitivity_points: Completeness of key revocation within the Cryptographic Erasure Engine
Audit logging to prove deletion without retaining underlying personal data
tradeoffs: Cryptographic erasure provides instant irreversible compliance but prevents retrospective data recovery
